A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, five figures, and appendices—A–I in v1 and A–K in v2—support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds and proofs, including its appendices. References to physical experiments concern cited work, not original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its added squared-loss and noisy-feedback results are mathematical derivations, not experiments or simulations.

M1.justification: The halving-tree, von Neumann-tree, and matrix-completion constructions are retained. v2 extends theoretical settings and guarantees without introducing a new learning algorithm or changing an existing algorithm's steps.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or executes training or evaluation tasks. The added ε-realizable setting is analyzed mathematically.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods. Discussions of earlier algorithms and bounds are theoretical comparisons and citations.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols. The new loss and feedback assumptions define theoretical learning settings rather than executed evaluations.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness experiments, error analyses, or empirical case studies. The restricted-state constructions are theoretical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's stochastic-feedback distributions are theoretical assumptions, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither contains measured performance values or empirical result entries. Changes to mathematical guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 adds an L2 regret derivation with T ≤ 4^n (Corollary 4.2, Appendix F) and a noisy ε-realizable regret definition and proof (Section 5.1, Appendix H), replacing v1's exact-label realizability formulation. It removes v1 Corollary 5.4's mistake-bound statement while retaining the principal shattering constructions and smoothed bound. The cited tomography scaling also changes from ~Θ(Nr²/ε²) to ~Θ(Nr/ε²).

C1.justification: v1 explicitly limits its central regret-equivalence claim to L1 loss. v2's Main Contributions adds L2 tightness, qualified by T ≤ 4^n in Corollary 4.2, and reformulates the realizability contribution around noisy ε-realizable feedback with asymptotically ε-independent regret. The principal pure-versus-mixed equivalence and smoothed-learning claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation attributing rank insensitivity to density-matrix constraints and discusses possible covariance, kernel, and Laplacian applications (Section 6). It motivates noisy feedback and discusses remaining room to improve the L2 bound. Conversely, v1 Remark 5.2's explicit discussion of the δ–n restriction disappears, although that condition remains in the theorem statements.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation settings, computing-resource information, or code/data access instructions. Added proof details do not introduce implementation or experimental reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning toward classical matrix learning through Alon, Bartlett, Srebro–Shraibman, Tsuda, and Shen and colleagues. It also adds Bansal et al. and Raza et al., while removing citations including Chen–Wang and Zhang et al. Section 3 newly emphasizes that many intermediate results are recoverable from prior work and positions the unified proof framework as the contribution.

P1.justification: v2 replaces the roadmap with Main Contributions, integrates related work into the introduction, rewrites and separates quantum background, and adds substantial proof intuition. It groups noisy and smoothed learning into an Extensions section and moves coupling material to Appendix J. These are extensive narrative and structural changes beyond theorem additions.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, title/author arrangement, typography, and headers. Figures 1–2 are placed side by side, Figure 3 changes from vertical to horizontal, and the partial-matrix diagram moves from main-text Figure 4 to appendix Figure 5. The same five underlying diagrams remain; no empirical plots or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves organization and adds explicit noisy-feedback analysis, but its newly emphasized L2 claim has unresolved proof support. Appendix F uses ±1 labels despite Section 2.2's [0,1] label space and substitutes I_N/N although Corollary 4.2 restricts hypotheses to pure states. These discrepancies make the net quality effect of the broader claims and clearer exposition uncertain.
